notes.title: Cassette Beasts Roundup Blog #1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/078639461e8b2b60bf11882a372cebf4a6c4f354.png[/img]
[h1]Welcome to Cassette Beasts - Roundup #1[/h1]

Hey folks, Tom and Jay here -- we're the duo behind Cassette Beasts! Cassette Beasts is our "dream game", an open-world monster-fusing RPG!

[i]"I don't know how best to break the news. You're stuck here. We all are."[/i]

The player begins the game having washed ashore on the beaches of New Wirral, and you soon learn of the predicament you are in. New Wirral holds many environments, dangers and secrets. On your quest to find your way back home, you'll explore the island at your own pace.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/b246da5b0ed2e091ff17613c9d371db78c5d3b88.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Harbourtown[/h2]
Harbourtown is the home for all residents of the island, and is a place you'll be returning to often. Built as a community that accepts everyone, Harbourtown is a place you can:
[list]
[*] Heal up without having to use wood for a campfire
[*] Swap out your adventuring partner for another
[*] Catch up on the latest town gossip
[*] Exchange resources for new moves to use in battle
[*] And more!
[/list]
The residents of Harbourtown may be strangers at first, but the more you get to know them, the more you'll learn about this strange world you've found yourself in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/32f0051dff5a47b717bf27019af7afc731303aae.gif[/img]

[h2]Transformation[/h2]
If you've been following so far, you'll know that in the world of New Wirral, the residents transform using cassette players. Each cassette tape contains the essence of one monster form, that its listener can transform into to battle. But how does one obtain new monster forms?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/b716d202b0c66fc6afb3223ff0f666c621a0a99e.png[/img]

[h2]Recording[/h2]
The built-in microphone on the cassette players can be used to record the essence of a wild monster. This isn't straightforward and it comes with its own risks. In order to record a monster, you must return to human form - which means you are vulnerable to attack.
A successful recording will net you a new tape, and a new bestiary entry for your collection if you've not obtained this monster form before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/730235c63fc0a2303b4f8e9a86869e6ef0c2ac06.png[/img]

[h2]Stickers[/h2]
You and your partner are able to act in battle using stickers - a list of actions that you can trigger on your turn. Each monster has a certain number of slots available to assign stickers, and monster forms are limited in which stickers they are able to use.
All of these stickers can be assigned and removed from a monster tape without any cost, so you are free to experiment to find the best loadouts for your monster forms!
There's one more cool thing to mention when talking about stickers - you can get uncommon and rare variants!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/74a94e669e3d38fcff06eae0aecdb56fcf5f4bc8.png[/img]

[h2]Fusion[/h2]
When you and your partner fuse in battle, you combine into a powerful and unique Fusion form!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/8e7005c206b0e5554481b09a648257112854c634.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/6ab22e31700e49e5390b3850effa281033806644.png[/img]

How does this affect your move list, then? Well, you get both move pools at once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/d642e30bbfedfd77f35c290c533cca9d2800c8b6.png[/img]
Not only does it mean you can use any of the active moves assigned to either monster used to create your fusion form, but your passive moves will all still be able to trigger. You can have very interesting and versatile fusion forms as a result of this!
There are also unique "Fusion Power" moves that you can obtain when fused!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Next Time[/h2]
Thank you for taking the time to read our quick roundup of some of the features and systems in Cassette Beasts. To see more in detail, you can view the individual posts below.
If you want to ask any questions, feel free to visit the official [url=https://discord.com/invite/byttenstudio]Discord[/url] and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ByttenStudio]Twitter![/url]

notes.title: Cassette Beasts Blog #4 - Show us (your) moves!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/c4b5030a85f72476c5c2a72f6f5f49824feaae39.png[/img]

Welcome back! Today we're going to look at combat and moves in [i]Cassette Beasts[/i] - since battling monsters as monsters is at the core of the gameplay, we thought it'd be a good idea to dive into how it works!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Stickers[/h2]

You and your partner are able to act in battle using stickers - a list of actions that you can trigger on your turn. Each monster has a certain number of slots available to assign stickers, and monster forms are limited in which stickers they are able to use.

Let's take a look!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/74a94e669e3d38fcff06eae0aecdb56fcf5f4bc8.png[/img]
[i]A look at Bansheep's default full sticker set. [/i]

You'll notice that most moves here have a set of orange squares next to them: these represent the number of Action Points, or [b]AP[/b], it costs to use them. A party member gains 2 AP per turn, so you have some choices to make - do you spend your AP on a low cost move such as "Sharpen" this turn, or perhaps use a no-cost move like "Smack" in order to use a [i]stronger [/i]move next turn? You'll be making choices like this a lot as you fight: it's time to think strategically!

You'll also notice that one of the moves here does [i]not [/i]have a cost, and instead is listed as "passive". Some stickers have their own trigger conditions in battle, such as losing a certain amount of HP.

All of these stickers can be assigned and removed from a monster tape without any cost, so you are free to experiment to find the best loadouts for your monster forms!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Fusion[/h2]

Wait, didn't we say last time we'd show what these two looked when fused?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/8e7005c206b0e5554481b09a648257112854c634.gif[/img]
[i]Oh yeah, we did![/i]

When you and your partner fuse in battle, you combine into a powerful and unique Fusion form!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/6ab22e31700e49e5390b3850effa281033806644.png[/img]
[i]Banlope! Like, Bansheep + Thwackalope! That makes sense.[/i]

How does this affect your move list, then? Well, you get [i]both[/i] move pools at once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/d642e30bbfedfd77f35c290c533cca9d2800c8b6.png[/img]
[i]That's a lot of moves![/i]

Not only does it mean you can use any of the active moves assigned to either monster used to create your fusion form, but your passive moves will all still be able to trigger. You can have very interesting and versatile fusion forms as a result of this! 

There are also unique "Fusion Power" moves that you can obtain when fused, but we can talk about that another time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

There's one more cool thing to mention when talking about stickers - you can get [i]uncommon [/i]and [i]rare [/i]variants. Let's have a look at this move set for Palangolin:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/b1c3afba28891cd38f4c311fe10551c7e764ee1b.png[/img]
[i]Palangolin can use Toxic Stab AND Battery? That's pretty versatile.[/i]

Do you see how "Sharp Edges" is displayed with green text? That means it is [i]uncommon[/i], and has a bonus effect that is listed on the move description. In this case, it heals 7% of the owner's HP when activated. There are lots of different bonus effects, and they differ depending on the kind of move and its rarity. You might find yourself coming across some extra useful versions of commonly-found move stickers!

This status page also displays the stat balance of the monster form. Palangolin is better at melee combat, which is no surprise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Next Time[/h2]

Wow, there sure are a lot of moves with many different elemental types. I wonder how they all work? I guess we'll find out next time! If you want to ask any questions, feel free to visit the official [url=https://discord.com/invite/byttenstudio]Discord[/url] and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ByttenStudio]Twitter[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/b96b97436bf6d2f60b85fecea3642f64908a5339.gif[/img]
[i]What would these two look like when fused? Find out next time![/i]

notes.title: Cassette Beasts Blog #3 - Monter...forms?
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/4ed32502c1b9d64a984c9f834a0c0cb651dabec9.png[/img]

This week, we're going to take a look at the ins and outs of monster transformation. Cassette tapes? Recording? What does it all mean?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Transformation[/h2]

If you've been following so far, you'll know that in the world of New Wirral, the residents transform using cassette players. Each cassette tape contains the essence of one [b]monster form[/b], that its listener can transform into to battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/b716d202b0c66fc6afb3223ff0f666c621a0a99e.png[/img]

transforming into a monster is the best way to fight back against the hostile monsters that roam this strange island! But how does one obtain new monster forms?

[h2]Recording[/h2]

The built-in microphone on the cassette players can be used to record the essence of a wild monster. This isn't straightforward and it comes with its own risks. In order to record a monster, you must return to human form - which means you are vulnerable to attack.

When you select the "Record" option in battle, you are given the option to choose a blank tape, and also the wild monster you wish to target. For the next turn of combat, the party member who is recording will return to human form, establishing a recording connection with the target.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/730235c63fc0a2303b4f8e9a86869e6ef0c2ac06.png[/img]
[i]Let's try and record a copy of this monster! Wait... is this piracy?[/i]

A percentage meter will appear above the heads of the target - this displays the chance of a successful recording. This likelihood can be raised or lowered before the turn ends, and is influenced by several things:
[list]
[*]The quality of the blank tape
[*]How much HP they had when recording begins
[*]How much damage is done to the target in rest of the turn
[*]How much damage is done to the recorder in the rest of the turn
[/list]
A successful recording will net you a new tape, and a new bestiary entry for your collection if you've not obtained this monster form before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/d6841368641b1f30fbb5f94957810236e644b420.png[/img]
[i]It may may look cute, but the Thwackalope's big makeshift club gives it access to some strong attacks.[/i]

That's the gist of it! Whilst most monster forms can be obtained from wild monsters, there are some that you might have to add to your collection through other means.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Gamescom[/h2]

Did you catch our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1321440/view/3410932054048704973]announcement[/url]? We're bringing a demo of Cassette Beasts to Gamescom 2022! [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/f952d67e0d5da8c2a401c87caf2f6fbe7ea7c8ea.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h2]Next Time[/h2]

For our next blog post, we'll look at the battle system with more depth, as well as how fusion works. Which begs the question - what does a fusion of Thwackalope and Bansheep look like?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/8e7005c206b0e5554481b09a648257112854c634.gif[/img]

As always, you can come chat to us on the official [url=https://discord.com/invite/byttenstudio]Discord [/url]and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ByttenStudio]Twitter[/url]!
Until next time!

notes.title: Cassette Beasts Blog #2 - New Wirral, Home Sweet... Home?
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/9483adfe7a12df060e0b01713e76f51ace0a0efb.png[/img]

We're back from summer hiatus (and sunny weather) to take another dive into [i]Cassette Beasts[/i]! In today's blog post, we wanted to take a look at the world of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h1]New Wirral[/h1]

The game is set on the island of New Wirral, a mysterious land inhabited by, as you might have guessed, [i]beasts[/i]. The player begins the game having washed ashore on the beaches of New Wirral, and you soon learn of the predicament you are in.

New Wirral holds many environments, dangers and secrets. On your quest to find your way back home, you'll explore the island at your own pace.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/1a2d5b990a5caae116ca8010401012ade3e554be.png[/img]

It must be said that there is nothing unique about your arrival - the other residents of the island [i]also[/i] found their way there in the same way. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/9fc335d2da269e2bd702883582a73ac1ead84483.png[/img]

When the first people to find themselves on New Wirral arrived, they eventually founded a town - a town that stands to this very day! Which is...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h1]Harbourtown[/h1]

Harbourtown is the home for all residents of the island, and is a place you'll be returning to often. Built as a community that accepts everyone, Harbourtown is a place you can:

[list]
[*] Heal up without having to use wood for a campfire
[*] Swap out your adventuring partner for another
[*] Catch up on the latest town gossip
[*] Exchange resources for new moves to use in battle
[*] And more!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/32f0051dff5a47b717bf27019af7afc731303aae.gif[/img]
[h3]Rumours[/h3]

In regards to gossip, the townsfolk will often have rumours to impart to you. These can tip you off about new monster locations, quests and other information that will help you explore the island!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/1e205d2141811fa53d65430076436371d04c88ad.gif[/img]

[h3]Town Hall[/h3]

The Town Hall is the HQ of the rangers, who help keep the island safe. Here you can unlock certain unique upgrades for your cassette player that help you in battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/1d7a2b12c0ff12b731c7f63d071cdb72accc6692.png[/img]

The residents of Harbourtown may be strangers at first, but the more you get to know them, the more you'll learn about this strange world you've found yourself in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

That's all for this blog! If you have any further questions, why not join our [url=https://discord.gg/HUWjFX3]growing Discord community[/url]? There you can get the latest info on Cassette Beasts, as well as participate in exclusive events and gameplay streams!

We have lots of exciting news coming soon, so keep your eyes peeled!

notes.title: Cassette Beasts Steam Blog #1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/ff1e87987e3632a6bf988ea3d1272d19c80d0738.png[/img]

Hey folks, Tom and Jay here -- we’re the duo behind Cassette Beasts! Cassette Beasts is our “dream game”, an open-world monster-fusing RPG!

[i][b]“I don’t know how best to break the news. You’re stuck here. We all are.”[/b][/i]

Welcome to New Wirral, a remote island inhabited by creatures you’ve only dreamed of, nightmares you hopefully haven’t, and a cast of brave folks who use cassette tapes to transform for battle. To find a way home you’ll need to explore every inch of the island, and record monsters to tape to gain their abilities!

But you’re not alone. You’ll make many good friends along the way, and battle alongside them. Friendships are critical to your progress -- the closer you are to your companions, the stronger you become when you fuse with them!

We thought we’d start things off with an introduction to the game and its features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/b246da5b0ed2e091ff17613c9d371db78c5d3b88.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h1]Monsters[/h1]

The island of New Wirral is teeming with monsters, but by recording them with your cassette player, you can transform into your own monster forms for battle! Your monster forms can be equipped with powerful and tactical battle moves and can evolve into even more powerful forms. With 120 monsters to encounter and record, there are many battles ahead of you!

[h1]Fusion[/h1]

Cassette Beasts’ headline feature is its Fusion System, which allows it to generate unique, fully-animated sprites for any combination of two monsters. Any two of the 120 monster forms can be fused, creating over fourteen thousand unique fusions. You can see how this works with a select few monsters on our [url=https://www.cassettebeasts.com/fusion/]web-based demo[/url].

Fusion works like a temporary evolution during battle. After transforming your player character and chosen (human) companion into monsters, you can fuse them into a single fighter. From then on, until you un-fuse, the two characters work as one, with combined elemental types, combined stats, and access to both sets of moves.

Some of your opponents have access to this ability too!

[h1]Open World[/h1]

New Wirral might be a small island, but it’s densely packed with secrets you can explore at your own pace.

Once recorded, certain monster forms allow you to use unique abilities while in human form. You’ll need these to help you get around, solve puzzles, and locate dungeons. Glide, fly, swim, dash, or turn magnetic!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h1]FAQ[/h1]

We’ve compiled some answers to the most common questions we are asked into an FAQ!

[h2]Who are we?[/h2]

We’re Bytten Studio, and we’re making Cassette Beasts because it’s the game we want to play! We’re lifelong fans of the monster-collecting RPG genre, and are keen to give it our own weird twist.

You might have heard of the first game we released as a studio -- Lenna’s Inception, which has been in several charity bundles -- or the other games we worked on before that: Stardew Valley, Starbound, and Wargroove. Cassette Beasts’ fusion system draws on all of our experience in monster design, procedural systems and making memorable characters.

[h2]When & where is it coming out?[/h2]

Cassette Beasts is being published by Raw Fury, and is coming to Windows and Linux on Steam, as well as Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Game Pass, and Nintendo Switch. No release date has been announced yet.

[h2]Is there multiplayer?[/h2]

We’ve envisioned Cassette Beasts as a single-player experience first, rather than as a competitive or online multiplayer game. However, there is local co-op integration where a second player is able to take control of the companion character both in the world and in battle!

[h2]Will we be releasing the OST?[/h2]

Yes, we aim to have the OST available on launch!

[h2]Will there be a demo?[/h2]

We’d like to have a public demo if the timing worked out right for it! Watch this space.

[h2]Is there a wiki?[/h2]

We're working on an official wiki! It's not quite ready to go live yet but it will be soon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37755710/a3fb3b149540b85b7b653fc5d8b96c0986403d25.png[/img]

[h1]What's Next?[/h1]

We’re aiming to post more updates like this to Steam so stay tuned for future blog posts and let us know in the comments what you’d like us to cover!

Click the Wishlist and Follow buttons on Cassette Beasts’ store page to help support us! You can also join our [url=https://discord.gg/HUWjFX3]growing Discord community[/url] to be a part of exclusive streams, Q&A sessions, and keep abreast of the latest info.
